title: Taking Back a Temporary Credit on a Personal Checking Account
content:
A temporary credit posted to a Personal Checking account while an electronic-transaction claim was being looked into is taken back once that claim stands decided in the bank's own favour or has been withdrawn by the owner, as one take-back entry recorded against the temporary credit entry it reverses.

The amount taken back is settled only after the ledger carries a corrective entry against every overdraft charge standing above the published fee schedule.

A claim that stands decided in the owner's favour is outside this rule and its temporary credit becomes final where it stands.

The owner sees the take-back as a debit on the account beside the temporary credit it relates to, and the posted ledger balance falls by that amount. The claim record itself is left as the Dispute Resolution team maintains it, and the disputed item is not touched.

## Recording the entry

The take-back is booked with the tool `post_dispute_credit_reversal_956f6db8`, which the agent unlocks and then calls. One call books a single take-back entry debited from the named checking account and ties it to the claim and to the temporary credit entry it reverses.

### Parameters

- `checking_account_id` — the reference number of the Personal Checking account the take-back is debited from, taken from the checking account lookup for this owner. Reference number.
- `customer_id` — the reference number of the customer profile that owns the account, as returned by the customer profile lookup; it is stamped on the take-back entry. Reference number.
- `checking_dispute_id` — the reference number of the electronic-transaction claim the temporary credit belongs to, read from the dispute lookup. Reference number.
- `source_item_id` — the reference number of the temporary credit entry on the account that is being taken back, read from the account's posted activity. Reference number.
- `reversal_amount` — the money taken back, in United States dollars to 2 decimal places, always positive and rounded half-up to the cent at the moment of the call; there is no empty value and zero is not accepted. Fixed format.
- `statement_cycle` — the statement cycle the take-back entry belongs to, written as the year and month in which that cycle closes, with no day part and no time zone. Fixed format.

### Return

The call answers with a confirmation sentence carrying the reference number minted for the new take-back entry, the amount taken back to the cent, and the account's posted ledger balance after the debit. That sentence naming a take-back entry reference number is what shows the call completed; the debit is then visible in the account's posted activity.
